solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marked unfinished cake thus?

parts.note: the clue's 'unfinished' gives the word not, as in a job not done
a cake left unfinished in this way has not been given its icing, so it is iced in the negative sense

explanation.surface: A baker grades a cake that has been left without its topping.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of a cake that is 'not iced', and run together those words make one word meaning observed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have marked something is to have observed or paid attention to it, a synonym.

clue.text: Writer covering thrashing by club

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece covering another sits on top of it

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for the whole writer
a lick is a sharp blow, so a thrashing in miniature

explanation.surface: An author is shown beating someone with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter has said this clue was written for a plural answer and fits the grid's singular answer only loosely; a lick is a single blow rather than a full thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for a lofted iron golf club, roughly the modern nine iron.

clue.text: Famous 14 lost tapes of Nazareth

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be found again in a new order

explanation.surface: Some recordings from Nazareth have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' refers to the answer at 14 across: someone who swings, and this jungle hero swings through the trees on vines.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs's jungle hero is a famous character who travels by swinging on vines.

clue.text: Socialist breaks company principles

indicators.note: the socialist breaks into the company, splitting its letters

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A left-wing member disrupts a firm's guiding values.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs, a statement of one's principles.

clue.text: Thingamys act raised endless gloom

parts.note: to act is to do

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
endless means the final letter of the word for gloom is cut off

parts.note: shadow means gloom or darkness

explanation.surface: A performance lifts a persistent depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the last letter off SHADOW to leave SHADO, and 'raised' turns that upward into ODAHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodahs and thingamys are both colloquial words for objects whose names escape you.

clue.text: Wet sheep died on sack

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
a ewe is a female sheep
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A soaked sheep has expired on a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedew is to wet with drops, as dew does, so bedewed means moistened.

clue.text: Permit loan to be withdrawn? I can't answer that

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word for loan runs backwards

parts.note: a sub is a loan or advance on wages
a quiz contestant who cannot answer says pass

explanation.surface: A borrower asks whether a loan will be cancelled and gets an evasive reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be withdrawn' turns SUB into BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus pass is a permit allowing its holder to travel on buses, often free or cheaper.

clue.text: Pickpocket's not sure, missing half of change

parts.note: a diver is old slang for a pickpocket, who dives into pockets; the 's adds an S

indicators.note: missing tells us a piece of the word for unsure goes absent

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or not sure
half of the doubled pair of letters in the word for unsure is one of them

explanation.surface: A thief is uncertain and has lost half the loose change he took.
explanation.walkthrough: IFFY has a pair of Fs; 'missing half' drops one of them to leave IFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To diversify is to vary or branch out, a kind of change.

clue.text: Beef dish gives advantage to calves protected by these?

parts.note: beef Wellington is fillet of beef baked in pastry
to boot is an old verb meaning to benefit or avail, as in 'what boots it?'

explanation.surface: A beef recipe benefits young cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calves' looks like young cattle beside the beef dish, but it means the backs of the legs, which wellingtons (tall rubber boots) cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington boots are tall waterproof boots that come up to the knee and cover the lower legs.

clue.text: One chiding a medical student

definitions.meaning: someone who dresses another down, that is scolds them
a student who assists a surgeon by dressing wounds

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing down means scolding, and a dresser was a medical student assisting with surgical dressings.

clue.text: Noted locksmith?

parts.note: noted suggests set to musical notes, and a locksmith here works with locks of hair, so a famous musical hair-cutter

explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's opera is about a famous barber, a man who cuts hair and appears in music.

clue.text: Playing to Marian, a loved woman

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Marian plays to someone she adores.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, the woman someone is in love with.

clue.text: Hackney's governor wants clean energy promoted

indicators.note: promoted means the energy letter is moved up to an earlier place

parts.note: to rinse is to clean with water
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A London borough's leader wants green power given priority.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough, but a hackney is a horse for riding or driving; reins govern it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins control a horse, governing its direction and speed.

clue.text: Before cry for help, recognises wife's not in Cretan town

indicators.note: before places the shortened word ahead of the cry for help
not in means the wife's letter is absent from the word for recognises

parts.note: to know someone is to recognise them
W is the abbreviation for wife; 'wife's not in' means wife is not in
SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: A man recognises that his wife is absent and calls for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' removes W from KNOWS, leaving KNOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Knossos is an ancient site on Crete, home of the Minoan palace.

clue.text: Chap pulled back on southern course

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it, so the S comes last

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, a chap
drew means pulled, as in drew back a curtain

explanation.surface: A man retreats onto a course in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrews in Scotland is famous for its Old Course, the home of golf.

clue.text: Troubadour touring with one after the other

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the singer goes around the letter for with

parts.note: a troubadour was a medieval singer

explanation.surface: A minstrel travels about, accompanied, taking turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one after the other' looks like 'in sequence', but 'the other' is a British euphemism for sex, so it means someone after sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A person seeking sexual partners freely is after 'the other', British slang for sex.

clue.text: Unforeseen difficulty in appeal by female to cut funeral cloth

indicators.note: the appeal and female letters cut into the funeral cloth, splitting it

parts.note: a pall is the cloth spread over a coffin
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A woman's charm intrudes on a funeral drape.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or unsuspected difficulty, originally a concealed trap pit.

clue.text: Chose to be fattened up

definitions.meaning: to plump for something is to choose it
to plump something is to make it plumper, rounder or fatter

explanation.definitionFit: Plumped for means opted or selected, while to plump also means to fill out or fatten.

clue.text: I'm spotted, but never in a changing room

definitions.text: I'm spotted, but never in a changing room

parts.words: I'm spotted, but never in a changing room
parts.note: a speaker with spots who is never in a changing room: the proverbial animal that cannot change its spots

explanation.definitionFit: A leopard is a spotted big cat, and proverbially it cannot change its spots.

clue.text: Famous loner reportedly retiring to get engaged

parts.note: shy means retiring or reserved
to lock is to engage, as gears or mechanisms do

explanation.surface: A recluse is shy about getting engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loner reportedly' sounds like 'loaner': someone who lends money, the moneylender in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock is Shakespeare's famous moneylender, a lender of cash whose name means a ruthless creditor.

clue.text: Convertible plastic container is upset

parts.note: plastic means pliable, soft

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A plastic tub has fallen over.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft-top is a convertible car with a folding fabric roof.

clue.text: Might you see Kent, flying from this planet?

definitions.text: Might you see Kent, flying from this planet?

parts.words: Might you see Kent, flying from this planet?
parts.note: Kent is not the English county but Clark Kent, Superman, who came flying from his home world

explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is Superman's home planet in the comics, from which he was sent to Earth.

clue.text: Trap, note, in second Gunpowder Plot

indicators.note: the note sits inside the other letters
second picks the second letter of Gunpowder

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, what one plots towards
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A trap is set in the second gunpowder conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap in plumbing is the bent section of pipe that holds water. Some solvers instead read N (note) in BED (plot), after U.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-bend is the curved pipe under a sink that traps water to block sewer smells.

clue.text: Out of supply with drug, thug turns gofer

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available
ice is slang for crystal methamphetamine

indicators.note: turns means the word for thug is reversed

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout or thug

explanation.surface: A thug, cut off from supply of drugs, becomes an errand boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer runs errands, the job of a junior office worker.

clue.text: Boasted over English town

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, England.

clue.text: Unexpectedly defeated star that's opted out after training,

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the training letters

parts.note: a pip is a star on an army officer's shoulder
PE is physical education, training

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A star loses unexpectedly after quitting training.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten at the last moment, as a horse caught on the line, is losing unexpectedly.

clue.text: Idle suspect was late coming round

indicators.note: coming round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: the late are the dead, so was late means died
sus is British slang for suspect

explanation.surface: An idle suspect turned up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle machinery is not in use, the same as disused.

clue.text: Continue to oppress only the central characters

indicators.note: the central characters means the letters in the middle of the phrase

explanation.surface: Only the main characters are oppressed in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on means to continue determinedly, carry on.
